en: But however null these abstractions and the relation of externality arising from them may be, the moment of the negatively absolute, or of infinity, which in this example is designated as determinative in the relation of crime and punishment, is a moment of the absolute itself and must be shown in absolute ethical life, and we shall grasp the many-robed character of the absolute form, or of infinity, in its necessary moments and show how it determines the shape of absolute ethical life, from which the true concept and the relation of the practical sciences will result.

Since here it depends first of all on the determination of the relations contained herein, and thus the side of infinity must be brought out, we presuppose the positive, that the absolute ethical totality is nothing other than a people, which will also become clear already from the negative that we are considering here, in the following moments of it.
zh: 但无论这些抽象以及由之产生的外在性关系多么空虚，那个在眼前这个例子里被指认为罪行与刑罚之关系中起规定作用的环节、即否定的绝对者或无限性的环节，都是绝对者自身的环节，必须在绝对伦理中揭示出来，而我们将在其必然的诸环节中把握并指明绝对形式或无限性的多重形态，指明它们如何规定绝对伦理的形态，真正的概念以及各实践科学的关系就将由此得出。
由于这里首先取决于对其中所包含的这些关系的规定，因而必须把无限性这一面挑出来，我们就预先设定那个肯定的东西：绝对伦理的总体性不外是一个民族；这一点也会从我们在此考察的那个否定的东西上、在它的接下来几个环节中弄清楚。

en: In absolute ethical life, now, infinity or the form as the absolutely negative is nothing other than the subduing itself, grasped a moment ago, taken up into its absolute concept, in which it relates not to individual determinacies but to the whole actuality and possibility of these, namely life itself, so that the matter is equal to the infinite form, but in such a way that the positive of this matter is the absolutely ethical, namely belonging to a people, the being-one with which the individual demonstrates in the negative, through the danger of death alone, in an unambiguous way.

Through the absolute identity of the infinite, or of the side of the relation, with the positive, the ethical totalities, such as peoples are, take shape, constitute themselves as individuals and thereby place themselves as single over against single peoples; this position and individuality is the side of reality, thought without it they are thought-things; it would be the abstraction of the essence without the absolute form, which essence would precisely thereby be essenceless.

This relation of individuality to individuality is a relation and therefore a doubled one: the one the positive, the calm equal coexistence of both in peace, the other the negative, the exclusion of one by the other; and both relations are absolutely necessary.
For the second we have grasped the rational relation as a subduing taken up into its concept, or as absolute formal virtue, which is bravery.

It is through this second side of the relation that the necessity of war is posited for the shape and individuality of the ethical totality - war which, because in it there is the free possibility that not only individual determinacies but the completeness of these as life is annihilated, and indeed for the absolute itself or for the people, likewise preserves the ethical health of peoples in their indifference towards determinacies and towards becoming accustomed to them and their hardening, just as the movement of the winds keeps the lakes from the putrefaction into which a lasting calm would plunge them, as a lasting or even an eternal peace would plunge the peoples.
zh: 在绝对伦理中，作为绝对否定的东西的无限性或形式，不外就是刚才以概念把握到的那个制服本身被纳入了它的绝对概念之中，在这个概念里它并不牵涉个别的诸规定性，而是牵涉这些规定性的全部现实性和可能性、即生命本身，于是质料与无限的形式是相等的，只不过这种相等是这样：它的肯定面就是绝对伦理的东西，即属于一个民族，而个体是在否定的东西中、仅仅通过死亡的危险，才以毫不含糊的方式表明自己与这个民族的合而为一。
通过无限性、即关系这一面与肯定的东西的绝对同一性，那些伦理的总体性——各民族就是这样的总体性——才形成起来，把自己构成为个体，并因此作为单个的总体性与各个单个的民族相对而立；这种位置和个体性是实在性这一面，离开这一面来想，它们就是思想之物；那就会是没有绝对形式的本质的抽象，而这样的本质正因此就是无本质的。
这种个体性对个体性的关联是一种关系，因而是一种双重的关系：一个是肯定的，即两者在和平中平静而平等地并存；另一个是否定的，即一方被另一方排斥；而这两种关联都是绝对必然的。
对于后者，我们已经把理性的关系把握为一种被纳入其概念的制服，或者把握为绝对的形式美德，即勇敢。

正是通过关系的这第二个方面，对于伦理总体性的形态和个体性来说，战争的必然性被设定起来了——战争之所以如此，是因为在战争中存在着那种自由的可能性：被消灭的不只是个别的一些规定性，而是这些规定性作为生命的完整性，而且这是为绝对者自身、为民族而发生的——，战争同样保持着各民族的伦理健康，使它们对诸规定性、对诸规定性的习以为常和固定化保持无差别，就像风的运动使湖泊免于腐败，而持久的静止会把湖泊投入这种腐败之中，正如持久的、甚至永久的和平会把各民族投入其中一样。

en: With the negative of infinity just considered - because the shape of the ethical totality and its individuality is determined as a singleness directed outward, and its movement as bravery - the other side is immediately connected, namely the subsistence of the opposition.

One is infinity, negative, as the other is; the first is the negation of the negation, the opposition against the opposition, the second the negation and opposition itself in its subsistence as determinacies or manifold reality.

These realities in their pure inner formlessness and simplicity, or the feelings, are in the practical sphere feelings that reconstruct themselves out of difference and pass through the being-sublated of the difference-less self-feeling by way of an annihilation of intuitions and restore themselves - physical needs and enjoyments, which, again posited for themselves in the totality, in their infinite entanglements obey a necessity and form the system of the general mutual dependence with respect to physical needs and labor and accumulation for them and - this as science - the system of so-called political economy.

Since this system of reality is wholly in negativity and in infinity, it follows for its relation to the positive totality that it must be treated by the latter wholly negatively and must remain subjected to its domination; what is negative by its nature must remain negative and may not become something fixed.

In order to prevent it from constituting itself for itself and becoming an independent power, it is not enough to set up the propositions that everyone has the right to live, that in a people the universal must see to it that every citizen has his livelihood and that a complete security and ease of acquisition be present; this last, thought as an absolute fundamental proposition, would rather exclude a negative treatment of the system of possession and would let it have its way completely and establish itself absolutely.

But rather the ethical whole must keep it in the feeling of its inner nullity and hinder its shooting up, in relation to quantity and culture, into ever greater difference and inequality - which is what its nature tends toward - which is also brought about in every state, more unconsciously and in the shape of an external necessity of nature, of which it wished itself to be relieved, through ever greater expenditure of the state itself growing with the growth of the system of possession and correspondingly rising taxes and thus diminution of possession and increasing difficulty of acquisition, most of all through war, which brings what tends that way into manifold confusion, as well as through the jealousy of other estates and the oppression of trade, partly with its will, partly against its will through want of understanding and so on - to such degrees that the positive ethical life of the state itself allows independence from the purely real system and the assertion of the negative and restrictive attitude.
zh: 与刚才考察的无限性的否定面——因为伦理总体性的形态以及它的个体性被规定为一种对外的单一性，而它的运动被规定为勇敢——直接相结合着的，是另外那一面，即对立的持存。
一方和另一方一样是无限性、是否定的；前者是否定之否定，即反对对立本身的对立，后者则是作为诸规定性或杂多的实在性而持存着的否定和对立本身。

这些实在性在其纯粹的内在无形式和单纯性中，或者说这些感受，在实践领域中是从差别中重新把自己建构起来的、并且通过诸直观的消灭而穿过无差别的自我感受之被扬弃状态、又把自己重新恢复起来的感受，——也就是自然的种种需要和享受，它们又自为地被设定在总体性之中，在其无限的纠缠中服从一种必然性，并且就自然需要以及为这些需要而进行的劳动和积累而言构成普遍相互依赖的体系，而这一体系作为科学，就是所谓政治经济学的体系。
由于这个实在性的体系完全处在否定性和无限性之中，所以，就它同肯定的总体性的关系而言，结论就是：它必须被这一总体性完全否定地对待，并且必须始终服从于它的统治；按其本性是否定的东西，就必须保持为否定的，而不允许成为某种固定的东西。
为了防止它自为地把自己建构起来、成为一种独立的权力，仅仅立下这些命题是不够的：每个人都有生活的权利，在一个民族中普遍的东西必须操心让每个公民都有自己的生计、并且存在着完全的保障和获取的容易；而后面这一点如果被当作绝对的根本命题来想，倒会排除对占有体系的否定对待，反而让它完全自行其是、绝对地把自己固定下来。

毋宁说，伦理的整体必须让占有体系保持在对自身空虚的感受中，并且阻止它在量和教养方面向愈来愈大的差别和不平等蹿升——而它的本性正是趋向于此——，这种情况在每个国家中也都以如下方式被造成：更多地是无意识地、以某种外在自然必然性的形态（国家自己本来还希望摆脱这种必然性），通过国家自身随着占有体系的增长而不断增大的开支、以及相应地不断增加的赋税，从而占有的减少和获取的困难，尤其通过战争——战争把趋向于此的一切带入纷繁的混乱——，以及通过其他等级的嫉妒和对商业的压制，一部分是出于它们的意愿，一部分是违背它们的意愿、由于它们的无知等等，一直造成到这样的程度：国家自身的肯定伦理允许它独立于那个纯粹实在的体系，并坚持否定和限制的态度。

en: The reality in the relation in which it has just been considered and of which physical need, enjoyment, possession and the objects of possession and enjoyment are different sides, is pure reality; it expresses merely the extremes of the relation.
But the relation also contains an ideality, a relative identity of the opposed determinacies, and this can therefore not be positively absolute, but only formal.

Through the identity into which the real is posited in the relation of relations, possession becomes property and, more generally, particularity, including living particularity, is at the same time determined as a universal, whereby the sphere of right is constituted.
zh: 实在性在刚才考察它的那种关系中——自然需要、享受、占有以及占有和享受的对象，都是这一关系的不同方面——是纯粹的实在性；它仅仅表达这一关系的两极。
但这一关系也包含一种观念性、即对立诸规定性的一种相对同一性，而这样的同一性因此不可能是肯定地绝对的，而只能是形式的。
通过实在物在诸关系的关系中被置入的那种同一性，占有成为财产，而一般来说特殊性、包括活生生的特殊性，同时也被规定为一种普遍的东西，权利的领域就是由此建构起来的。

en: As for the reflex of the absolute in this relation, it has already been determined above, according to its negative side against the subsistence of the real and the determinate, as a subduing; according to the positive side for the subsistence of the real, indifference in this determinate material can express itself only as an external, formal equality, and the science that relates to this can only aim at determining partly the gradations of inequality, partly (so that this may be possible) the manner in which a living or inner thing is in general to be posited so objectively and externally that it is capable of that determination and calculation.
To this superficial appearance, the absolute reality of ethical life in this potency is restricted by the subsistence of the reality present in the opposition.

Not only does the equating and the calculation of inequality have its limits, on account of the fixed determinacy that includes an absolute opposition in itself, and run up against incommensurability as geometry does, but - because it [remains] wholly in the determinacy and yet cannot abstract as geometry can, but, since it is in living relations, absolutely always has whole convolutes of such determinacies before itself - also absolutely upon endless contradictions.

This contradicting of determinacies is indeed remedied and brought to an end in an intuition by fixing and holding fast to individual determinacies, whereby a decision can come about, which is still always better than that none comes about; for because in the matter itself there is nothing absolute, what is essential is properly the formal element, that a decision and determination is made at all.

But it is something quite different that a decision be made in this way according to true total justice and ethical life, which is precisely impossible through the fixing and absolute holding-fast to determinacies, possible only in their confusion and actual through immediate ethical intuition, which subjugates the determinacies posited as absolute and alone holds the whole fast. - It is, says Plato in his simple language about the two sides of the endless determining - that of the infinite taking-up of the qualities into the concept and that of the contradiction of their singleness with intuition and thereby among themselves - it is clear that the art of legislation belongs to the royal art; but the best is not that the laws be valid, but the man who is wise and royal, because the law is not able to prescribe perfectly what would be most exact and wholly universal, the most excellent and most just; because the inequalities of men and of actions and the never-resting of human things allow nothing self-same to be presented in any art, in no matter what matter, over all its sides and for all time.

But the law we see precisely directing itself at one and the same thing, like a stubborn and crude man who will let nothing happen against his ordinance and will not let anyone ask him about it when something different and better occurs to someone against the relation he has fixed; - it is therefore impossible that for the never-self-same the absolutely self-same should be good.235)
zh: 至于绝对者在这一关系中的映现，它已经在上文按其针对实在物和确定之物的持存而言的否定方面，被规定为一种制服；而按其针对实在物的持存而言的肯定方面，无差别在这种确定材料中只能表达为一种外在的、形式上的平等，与此相关的科学也只能着眼于：一方面规定不平等的各个层级，另一方面（为使这成为可能）规定一个活的东西或内在的东西究竟该怎样被设定得如此客观、如此外在，以至于它能够接受那种规定和计算。
由于对立中现成存在的实在性具有持存，伦理的绝对实在性在这一级次上就被限制在这样一种表面的现象上。
不仅由于那种自身包含着绝对对立的固定规定性，使平等化和对不平等的计算有其界限，并且像几何学一样撞上不可通约性，而且——因为它完全〔停留〕在规定性之中，却又不能像几何学那样进行抽象，而是由于它处在活生生的关系之中，绝对地总是有整堆这样的规定性摆在面前——还绝对地撞上无穷的矛盾。
在直观中，规定性之间的这种互相矛盾，确实可以通过确定并固守个别的一些规定性而得到补救、得到一个了结，由此可以产生一个决断，而这总比根本不作决断要好；因为既然事情本身中没有任何绝对的东西，那么真正本质性的东西其实倒是那个形式的东西：一般而言作出决断并被规定下来。

但另一回事是：按照真正的、总体的正义和伦理、以这种方式作出决断，而这种正义和伦理恰恰通过确定并绝对固守诸规定性而成为不可能，只有在诸规定性的混乱中才是可能的，并且通过直接的伦理直观才是现实的，这种直观制服那些被设定为绝对的规定性，并且唯独把整体固守住。——柏拉图用他朴素的语言，就无穷规定的两个方面——即把各种质无限地纳入概念这一方面，以及它们的单一性与直观、并由此与它们彼此之间的矛盾这一方面——说：很清楚，立法技艺属于王者技艺；但最好的并不是法律有效，而是那个智慧和有王者风范的人，因为法律无法把那种最精确、最普遍而言最卓越、最正义的东西完满地预先规定下来；因为人和行为的不平等，以及人事的永不停息，使得任何技艺都不能在任何事情上、在其所有方面、为一切时间把某种自身相同的东西呈现出来。
但我们看到，法律恰恰一味盯着同一个东西，就像一个固执而粗野的人，不允许有任何违背他的安排的事情发生，也不许有人就这一点来问他，即使别人针对他所确定的那层关系想到了别的、更好的东西；——所以，对于那从不自身相同的东西来说，那绝对自身相同的东西不可能是好的。235)

en: That there is a clinging to the thought that in this sphere of human things a being-in-itself and absolute determinate right and duty is possible comes from the formal indifference or the negatively absolute, which alone has a place in the fixed reality of this sphere and which is indeed in itself; but insofar as it is in itself, it is empty, or there is nothing absolute in it except precisely the pure abstraction, the wholly contentless thought of unity.

It is not, to be sure, an inference from experience so far, nor is it to be regarded as an accidental imperfection of the concrete and of the execution of an a priori true idea; rather it is to be recognized that what is here called an idea, and a hope of a better future in this matter, is in itself null, and that a perfect legislation, as well as a true justice corresponding to the determinacy of the laws, is in itself impossible in the concrete of judicial power.

As for the former, since the absolute is supposed to be in the determinacies as such, it is only the infinite, and it is the very same empirical infinity and in-itself endless determinability that is posited which is posited in the thought of a comparison of a determinate measure with an absolutely indeterminate line, or of a determinate line with an absolutely indeterminate measure, of the measuring of an infinite line or of the absolute dividing of a determinate line.

As for the other, among the likewise infinitely many and infinitely variously formed intuitions that are the object of the judicial, each is determined more manifoldly with the growing mass of determinations; that formation of distinctions by legislation makes each single intuition more distinguishable and more formed, and the extension of legislation is not an approximation to the goal of a positive perfection, which here, as shown above, has no truth, but only the formal element of increasing culture.

And in order that in this manifoldness the one of the judicial intuition of right and of judgment may organize itself, may become a true one and whole, it is absolutely necessary that every single one of the determinacies be modified, that is, precisely as an absolute, being-for-itself determinacy, for what it declares itself to be as law, be in part sublated, so that its being-absolute is not respected; and of a pure application there can be no question, for a pure application would be the positing of individual determinacies with the exclusion of others.
But through their being these likewise make the demand that they be taken into account, so that the counter-action be determined not by parts but by the whole, and be itself a whole.
To this clear and determinate cognition the empty hope and the formal thought both of an absolute legislation and of a pronouncing of right withdrawn from the inner of the judge must give way.
zh: 人们执着于这样一个想法，即在这个人事领域里可能有自在存在着的、绝对的、确定的权利和义务，这一点来自形式上的无差别、即否定的绝对者，它在这个领域固定的实在性中才有位置，而且它确实是在自在地存在着的；但就它自在而言，它是空的，或者说，在它那里除了纯粹抽象、这个完全没有内容的统一性思想之外，没有任何绝对的东西。
这当然不是从以往经验得出的推论，也不能被看作具体东西、以及某个 a priori 真的观念之实行所带有的偶然不完善；而是要认识到，这里被称为观念的东西、以及对此怀有的更好未来的希望，本身就是空虚的，并且一种完善的立法、以及一种与法律的规定性相应的真正正义，在司法权力的具体东西中本身是不可能的。
就前者而言，既然绝对者应当处在诸规定性本身之中，那它就是无限的东西，而被设定起来的正是那同一种经验性的无限性和自在的无穷规定性，就像在这样一种想法中被设定起来的那样：把一个确定的尺度与一条绝对不确定的线相比较，或者把一条确定的线与一个绝对不确定的尺度相比较，测量一条无限的线，或者绝对地分割一条确定的线。
就后者而言，那些同样无限多、并且以无限多样的方式形成起来的直观——它们是审判活动的对象——，每一个都随着规定性数量的增长而更多方面地被规定；立法所造成的那种区分使每一个别直观都更可区分、更有教养，而立法的扩展并不是向着一种肯定的完善性这一目标靠近——如上所示，这种完善性在这里并没有真理——，而只是教养不断增长这一形式的东西。
而为了在这种杂多中，对权利和判断的审判直观的那个一能够组织起来，成为一个真正的一和整体，就绝对必须让这些规定性中的每一个都被修改，也就是说，恰恰作为绝对的自为存在的规定性、就其把自己宣称为法律而言，被部分地扬弃，从而它的绝对存在不受到尊重；而纯粹的运用是谈不上的，因为纯粹的运用就是把个别的一些规定性设定起来、同时排除另一些。
但这些东西通过自己的存在，同样提出这样的要求：它们应当被顾及，以便反作用不是由各个部分、而是由整体来规定，并且本身是一个整体。
面对这种清楚而确定的认识，无论是那种空洞的希望，还是关于一种绝对立法、以及一种从法官内心中抽离出来的判决的形式想法，都必须让位。

en: It has been shown in the case of the system of reality under consideration that absolute ethical life must comport itself negatively toward it; in that system the absolute, as it appears under its fixed determinacy, is posited as negative absolute, as infinity, which presents itself over against the opposition as formal, relative, abstract unity; in that negative comportment hostile, in this one itself under its domination, in neither indifferent toward it.

But the unity which is indifference of the opposed and annihilates and conceives them in itself, and the unity which is only formal indifference, or the identity of the relation of existing realities, must themselves be absolutely as one, through the complete absorption of the relation into indifference itself; that is, the absolute ethical must organize itself completely as shape, for the relation is the abstraction of the side of shape.
In that the relation becomes absolutely undifferentiated in shape, it does not cease to have the nature of a relation; it remains a relation of organic to inorganic nature.
But as shown above, the relation, as the side of infinity, is itself twofold; at one time insofar as the unity or the ideal is the first and ruling, at the other insofar as the many or the real is.

According to that side it is properly in shape and in indifference, and the eternal restlessness of the concept or of infinity is partly, in the organization itself, consuming itself and surrendering the appearance of life, the purely quantitative, so that it eternally raises itself as its own seed-corn out of its ashes to new youth, — partly eternally annihilating its difference toward the outside and nourishing itself on the inorganic and producing it, calling forth out of indifference a difference, or a relation of an inorganic nature, and again sublating the same and consuming it as it consumes itself.
We shall presently see what this inorganic nature of the ethical is.

But secondly, in this side of the relation or of infinity, the persistence of what is annihilated is also posited; for precisely because the absolute concept is the opposite of itself, along with its pure unity and negativity the being of difference is also posited; or annihilation posits something that it annihilates, or the real, and so there would be an actuality and difference insurmountable for ethical life.

The individuality which, through the seat that infinity has here pitched in the whole force of its opposition, and is in the opposition not merely according to possibility but actu, according to actuality, would not be able to purify itself of difference and to receive itself into absolute indifference.

That both, the being-sublated of the opposition and its persistence, are not only ideal but also real, is in general the positing of a separation and a setting-apart, so that the reality in which ethical life is objective is divided into one part which is absolutely taken up into indifference, and into one in which the real as such is persisting, thus relatively identical, and bears in itself only the reflection of absolute ethical life.
Thereby a relation is posited of absolute ethical life, which is wholly indwelling in individuals and is their essence, to relative ethical life, which is likewise real in individuals.
The ethical organization cannot preserve itself pure in reality otherwise than in that the universal spread of the negative in it is checked and placed on one side.
How now indifference appears in the existing real and is formal ethical life has been shown above.

The concept of this sphere is the real practical, subjectively considered that of sensation or of physical need and enjoyment, objectively that of labour and of possession; and this practical, insofar as it can happen according to its concept, taken up into indifference, is the formal unity or the right that is possible in it, over both of which the third is as the absolute or the ethical.
But the reality of the sphere of relative unity, or of the practical and the juridical, is constituted in the system of its totality as an estate of its own.
zh: 在刚才考察的实在性系统那里已经表明，绝对伦理必然对它采取否定的态度；在这个系统里，绝对者——就它在该系统固定的规定性之下显现出来而言——被设定为否定的绝对者、被设定为无限性，而这无限性面对对立则表现为形式的、相对的、抽象的统一；它在那种否定的态度中是敌对的，在这种态度中却本身就处在对立的统治之下，而在两种态度中它对这个系统都不是无差别的。
但那种作为对立面的无差别、并在自身中消灭它们又以概念把握它们的统一，和那种仅仅是形式的无差别、或者说现存实在物之关系的同一性的统一，本身必须无条件地作为一体而存在，办法是把关系完全接纳进无差别本身之中；也就是说，绝对伦理的东西必须把自己完全组织为形态，因为关系是形态那一侧的抽象。
关系在形态中无条件地成为无差别的，却并不停止具有关系的本性；它仍然是有机的自然对无机的自然的关系。
但正如上面已经表明的，关系作为无限性的那一侧，本身是双重的；有时是就统一或观念物是第一位的、起统治作用的东西而言，有时则是就多或实在物是第一位的、起统治作用的东西而言。
按照那一侧，它其实就在形态中、在无差别中，而概念或无限性的永恒不安，一部分在组织本身中自己消耗自己，把生命现象、即纯粹量性的东西交出去，使它能作为它自己的种子从自己的灰烬中永远向着新的青春升起，——一部分则永远消灭自己向外的差别，靠无机物来滋养自己并生产无机物，从无差别中唤出一种差别、或者说一种无机自然的关系，然后又扬弃这关系，像消耗自己一样把它消耗掉。
我们马上就会看到，伦理的东西的这种无机的自然是什么。
但第二，在关系的这一侧、或者说无限性的这一侧，被消灭者的持存也被设定起来了，因为绝对概念恰恰是它自己的反面，所以随着它纯粹的统一和否定性，差别的存在也被设定起来；或者说，消灭活动设定某种它所消灭的东西、即实在物，这样就会有一种对伦理来说不可克服的现实性和差别。
这种个体性——由于无限性在这里以其对立的全部力量搭起的那个驻地，它不仅在可能性上、而且 actu、在现实性上处在对立之中——将无法使自己摆脱差别、并把自己接纳进绝对的无差别之中。
对立之被扬弃与对立之持存这两者不仅是观念的、而且是实在的，这本身一般就是设定一种分离和挑出，以致伦理在其中具有客观性的那种实在性被划分开，一部分绝对地被接纳进无差别之中，而另一部分则其中实在物作为这样的东西持存着、因而只是相对同一的，并且只在自身中带着绝对伦理的反映。
由此就设定起绝对伦理同相对伦理的一种关系，前者完全内居于个体之中、是他们的本质，后者同样在个体中是实在的。
伦理组织在实在性中无法以别的方式保持纯粹，除非它里面否定东西的普遍蔓延被遏制住并被搁到一边。
无差别在现存的实在物中如何显现、并如何是形式的伦理，上面已经表明过了。
这一领域的概念是实在的实践东西，从主观上看是感觉、或者说身体的需要和享受，从客观上看是劳动和占有；而这种实践东西，就它按照自己的概念能够发生而言，被接纳进无差别之中，就是形式的统一、或者说在它之中可能的权利，而在这两者之上，第三者就是绝对者或者说伦理的东西。
而相对统一这一领域、或者说实践东西和权利东西的领域的实在性，则在其总体性的系统中被构成为一个特有的等级。

en: Thus, according to the absolute necessity of the ethical, two estates form themselves, of which the one, as the estate of the free — the individual of absolute ethical life, whose organs the single individuals are and which, considered from the side of its indifference, is the absolute living spirit, and from the side of its objectivity the living movement and the divine self-enjoyment of this whole in the totality of individuals as its organs and members, while its formal or negative side must likewise be the absolute one, namely labour, which does not aim at annihilating particular determinacies but at death, and whose product is likewise not something singular but the being and preservation of the whole of the ethical organization.

To this estate Aristotle assigns as its business that for which the Greeks had the name πολιτεύειν, which expresses living in and with and for one's people, leading a universal life wholly belonging to the public, or philosophizing, — which two businesses Plato, in accordance with his higher vitality, does not want seen as separated but absolutely linked. — Then an estate of the unfree, which is in the difference of need and labour and in the right and justice of possession and property, whose labour aims at singularity and thus does not include within itself the danger of death.

To which the third estate must be counted, which in the crudeness of its non-formative labour has to do only with the earth as element, and whose labour has before it the whole of need in the immediate object without intermediate members, and is thus itself a solid totality and indifference like an element, and thereby, apart from the difference of the understanding of the second estate, preserves for itself its bodies and its spirit in the possibility of formal absolute ethical life, of bravery and of a violent death, and thus is able to increase the first estate in respect of mass and elementary essence. — These two estates relieve the first of the relation in which reality is fixed, partly in its resting, partly in its active relation, as possession and property and as labour, in the manner in which, in a way for the time being restricted to this, among the more recent peoples the acquiring class has gradually ceased to do military service, and bravery has purified itself into a particular estate, which is relieved by that of acquisition and for which possession and property are at least something contingent.

The constitution of that second estate, as regards its matter, Plato determines thus: that the royal art subdues and casts out through death and banishment and the ultimate disgrace those who are unable to become partakers of the brave and disciplined custom (and whatever else drives to virtue), but only of that which through its evil violent nature pushes toward godlessness and insolence and injustice; that the royal art, on the contrary, subjugates to the servile race the natures that lie in crudeness and lowliness238); and Aristotle recognizes as belonging to it that which through its nature is not its own but another's, which relates as body to a spirit239).
zh: 所以，按照伦理的绝对必然性，形成两个等级，其中第一个作为自由人的等级、即绝对伦理的那个个体，它的诸器官就是各个个体，而从它的无差别那一侧来看它是绝对活生生的精神、从它的客观性那一侧来看它是这整个东西在作为其器官和成员的诸个体的总体性中的活生生的运动和神圣的自我享受，但它的形式的一侧或否定的一侧同样必须是绝对的一侧，即劳动，这种劳动不是针对消灭各个规定性，而是针对死亡，它的产品同样不是个别的东西，而是伦理组织这个整体的存在和保持。

亚里士多德指定给这个等级作为其事务的，是希腊人用 πολιτεύειν 这个名字来称呼的东西，它表达的是在自己的民族之中、同自己的民族一起、为自己的民族而生活，过一种普遍的、完全属于公共事务的生活，或者说表达的是哲学思考，——而这两种事务，柏拉图按照他更高的生动性，不愿把它们分开，而要把它们无条件地联结起来看。 - 然后是一个不自由人的等级，它处在需要和劳动的差别之中，处在占有和财产的权利与公正之中，它的劳动针对的是个别性，因此并不包含死亡的危险。

第三个等级也必须算到它们之中，这个等级在其粗陋的、不事教养的劳动中只与作为元素的土地打交道，它的劳动在直接的对象中、不经过任何中间项地面对着需要的整体，因此本身就是一个像元素一样坚实的总体性和无差别，它由此在第二个等级的知性差别之外，为自己把自己的身体和自己的精神保持在形式的绝对伦理、即勇敢和一种暴力的死的可能性之中，因此能够按数量和元素性的本质来增加第一个等级。 - 这两个等级使第一个等级摆脱了那种关系，在那种关系中，实在性一部分在其静止的关联中、一部分在其活动的关联中，被固定为占有和财产、被固定为劳动，其方式就像在较晚近的诸民族中，以一种当时还局限于此的方式，营利的阶级逐渐停止服兵役，而勇敢则更纯粹地形成了一个特殊的等级，这个等级由营利的那个等级解除了[这种义务]，并且对它来说占有和财产至少是某种偶然的东西。

至于那第二个等级的构成，就其质料而言，柏拉图是这样规定的：王者的技艺用死亡、流放和最终的羞辱制服并抛出那些不能分有勇敢而有节制的习俗（以及别的什么把人引向德性的东西）、而只能分有那种由于其恶劣的暴力本性而把人推向不敬神、骄横和不义的东西的人，与此相反，王者的技艺则把处在粗陋和卑下之中的那些本性压制为奴隶的族类238)，而亚里士多德则把那种按其本性不是自己的、而是别人的东西、那种像身体对精神一样发生关系的东西，认作属于这个等级239)。

en: But the relation of this, which through its nature is another's and does not have its spirit in itself, to the absolutely self-dependent individuality, is capable according to its form of being twofold, namely either a relation of the individuals of this estate as particular to the individuals of the first as particular, or of universal to universal.

That relation of slavery has of itself disappeared in the empirical appearance of the universality of the Roman Empire; in the loss of absolute ethical life and with the degradation of the noble estate, the two previously particular estates have become equal to each other, and with the cessation of freedom slavery has necessarily ceased.

In that the principle of formal unity and of equality had to become valid, it has in general sublated the inner true difference of the estates and, to begin with, brought about neither the separation of estates posited above, still less the form of their separation conditioned by it, according to which they, under the form of universality, are related only as whole estate to whole estate in the relation of domination and dependence, so that also in this relation the two that are in the relation remain universal; whereas, by contrast, in the relation of slavery the form of particularity is the determining one of that relation, and it is not estate against estate but this unity of each part that is dissolved in the real relation, and the individuals are dependent on individuals.

The principle of universality and equality had first to take possession of the whole in such a way that it put a mingling of both estates in the place of a separation; in this mingling under the law of formal unity, the first estate is in truth wholly sublated and the second made into the sole people; the picture of which change Gibbon240) expresses in these lines: The long peace and the uniform rule of the Romans brought a slow and secret poison into the vital forces of the empire.
The sentiments of men were gradually brought to one level, the fire of genius extinguished, and even the military spirit evaporated.

Personal courage remained, but they no longer possessed this public courage, which is nourished by the love of independence, the sense of national honour, the presence of danger and the habit of commanding; they received laws and commanders from the will of their monarch, and the descendants of the boldest chiefs were content with the rank of citizens and subjects.

The minds striving higher gathered around the banner of the emperors, and the abandoned lands, deprived of political strength or unity, sank imperceptibly into the dull indifference of private life. — With this universal private life, and for the condition in which the people consists only of a second estate, the formal relation of right, which fixes and absolutely posits singleness, is immediately present, and the most complete development of the legislation relating to it has also formed and developed itself out of such depravity and universal degradation.

This system of property and right, which, for the sake of that fixedness of singularity, is in nothing absolute and eternal but wholly in the finite and formal, must, really separated and excluded from the noble estate, constitute itself in an estate of its own and then be able to expand here in its whole length and breadth.

To it belong partly the questions, subordinate in themselves and remaining in the formal, about the legal ground of possession, contract, etc., but partly in general the whole endless expansion of legislation over — as Plato lists the rubrics of these things — "these judicial objects of the contracts of individuals with individuals about things or handicrafts, as also of injuries and blows, arrangements about competence and appointments of judges, and where a levying or imposing of tolls on the markets and harbours is necessary, — as about which it is not worthy to prescribe to fine and good men, for they will of themselves easily find the many things that must be determined about it, if God gives them the blessing of a truly ethical constitution."

But where this is not the case, it follows that they spend their life in laying down and improving many such things, thinking that they will finally take possession of the best, — that they live like sick people who, out of intemperance, do not want to leave their bad diet and through the remedies effect nothing but to produce more manifold and greater illnesses, while they always hope that, if someone advises them of a remedy, they will become healthy from it.

Just as comical are those who give laws about the things cited and always improve on them, in the opinion that they will thereby reach an end, — unaware that they in fact, as it were, cut the Hydra to pieces."241) — "If it is now true that, with increasing unruliness and sickness in the people, the many courts open and no greater sign of a bad and shameful discipline can be found than that not only the bad and the craftsmen need excellent physicians and judges, but also those who pride themselves on having been brought up in a free culture are compelled to have a justice imposed on them by others as lords and judges and spend much time in courts with complaints and defences"242), — if this system must at the same time develop as a general condition there and destroy free ethical life, where the latter is mixed with those relations and is not originally separated from them and their consequences, then it is necessary that this system be taken up with consciousness, recognized in its right, excluded from the noble estate, and that an estate of its own be granted to it as its realm, in which it can establish itself and develop its complete activity in its confusion and in the sublation of one confusion by another.

Accordingly, the potency of this estate is determined thus: that it finds itself in possession in general and in the justice that is possible therein regarding possession, that it at the same time constitutes a coherent system, and that immediately through the fact that the relation of possession is taken up into formal unity, every individual, since he is in himself capable of a possession, relates to all as universal or as citizen, in the sense of bourgeois, and finds for the political nullity, according to which the members of this estate are private persons, the compensation in the fruits of peace and of acquisition and in the complete security of the enjoyment of the same, both insofar as it goes to the individual and to the whole of the same.

But the security for every individual goes to the whole insofar as he is relieved of bravery and removed from the necessity, which belongs to the first estate, of exposing himself to the danger of a violent death, which danger for the individual is the absolute insecurity of all enjoyment and possession and right.

Through this sublated mingling of the principles and the constituted and conscious separation of them, each receives its right, and only that is brought about which ought to be: the reality of ethical life as absolute indifference and at the same time of the very same as the real relation in the existing opposition, so that the latter is conquered by the former and that this conquering is itself made indifferent and reconciled, — which reconciliation consists precisely in the cognition of necessity and in the right that ethical life gives to its inorganic nature and to the subterranean powers, in that it surrenders and sacrifices to them a part of itself; for the power of sacrifice consists in the intuition and objectification of the entanglement with the inorganic, through which intuition this entanglement is dissolved, the inorganic is separated off and, recognized as such, is thereby itself taken up into indifference, while the living being, in that it lays into it what it knows as a part of itself and sacrifices it to death, has at the same time recognized its right and at the same time purified itself of it.
zh: 但这种按其本性属于别人、并且不在自身中拥有自己的精神的东西，同绝对独立的个体性的关系，按其形式则可能是双重的，即要么是这个等级的诸个体作为特殊者同第一个等级的诸个体作为特殊者的关系，要么是普遍者对普遍者的关系。
那种奴隶制的关系在罗马帝国的普遍性这一经验现象中自行消失了；在绝对伦理的丧失中、随着高贵等级的贬降，先前特殊的两个等级变得彼此相同了，而随着自由的终止，奴隶制也必然终止了。

由于形式统一和平等的原则必然要起作用，它一般地扬弃了各等级内部真正的差别，并且首先既没有造成上面所设定的等级分离，更没有造成由这种分离所制约的各等级分离的形式——按照这种形式，它们在普遍性的形式下只是作为整个等级同整个等级处在统治和依赖的关系中，以致在这种关系里，处在关系中的那两者也仍然是普遍的；相反，在奴隶制的关系里，特殊性的形式才是规定这种关系的东西，并且被解体的不是等级对等级，而是每个部分在实在的关系中的这种统一，各个个别者则依赖于个别者。
普遍性和平等的原则首先必须这样地占据整体，以致它用一种两个等级的混合取代了分离；在这种处于形式统一法则之下的混合中，第一个等级实际上被完全扬弃了，第二个等级则被弄成唯一的民族；对于这一变化，吉本240)用下面这些话描绘了它的图景：罗马人长久的和平和整齐划一的统治，把一种缓慢而隐秘的毒药带进了帝国的生命力之中。
人们的意向逐渐被带到同一个水平面上，天才的火焰被熄灭了，就连军事的精神也蒸发了。
个人的勇气还在，但他们不再拥有这种公共的勇气了，这种勇气是由对独立的热爱、民族荣誉感、危险的在场和发号施令的习惯滋养起来的；他们从自己君主的意志那里领受法律和统帅，而那些最胆大的首领的后代则满足于公民和臣民的地位。
那些向更高处努力的心聚集到皇帝的旗帜下，而那些被遗弃的地方，被剥夺了政治力量或统一，便不知不觉地沉入私人生活那种无精打采的漠然之中。 - 同这种普遍的私人生活一起，并且对于那种民族只由一个第二等级构成的状况来说，形式的权利关系——它把单个存在固定下来并绝对地设定起来——直接就存在了，而与之相关的立法的最完整的养成，也正是从这样一种败坏和普遍的贬降中形成和发展出来的。
这种财产和权利的系统，为了个别性的那种固定不变而完全处在有限和形式的东西之中、而不处在任何绝对和永恒的东西之中，它必须实在地区分开来、从高贵等级中排除出去，在一个特有的等级中把自己构成起来，并且在这里能够按它的整个长度和宽度展开。

属于它的，一部分是那些本身从属的、停留在形式东西之中的问题，即关于占有、契约等等的权利根据的问题，另一部分则一般地是立法的那整个无尽的扩展，涉及——如柏拉图列举这些事情的名目那样——“个人与个人之间关于物品或手工活的契约、以及侮辱和殴打这些司法对象，关于管辖权限和法官任命的规定，以及在市场和港口征收或设置关税的必要性，——而对于这些事情，向美好而善良的人作规定是不值得的，因为如果神给他们一个真正伦理的宪法的祝福，他们自己就会轻易找到必须对此规定下来的那许多东西。”
但如果不是这种情况，结果就是：他们把自己的生命用在规定和改进许多这类事情上，以为最终会占有最好的东西，——就是他们活得像病人一样，这些病人由于不节制而不愿离开自己糟糕的饮食调理，通过药物除了造成更多样、更严重的疾病之外什么也做不到，而他们却始终希望，只要有人给他们推荐一种药，他们就能靠这药健康起来。

同样滑稽可笑的是那些人，他们针对上面提到的那些事情制定法律并不断加以改进，以为这样就能达到一个终点，——却不知道他们实际上等于是在把九头蛇切成碎块。”241) —— “如果下面这一点是真的：随着民族中无节制和疾病的增长，许多法庭纷纷开门，而对于一种糟糕而可耻的管教来说，再也找不到比这更大的标志了，即不仅坏人和手工匠需要出色的医生和法官，而且那些自夸受过自由教养的人也不得不拥有一种由别人作为主人和法官加给他们的公正，并把许多时间花在法庭上控告和辩护”242)，——如果这个系统同时作为一种普遍状况必须在自由伦理同那些关系相混杂、并且没有原初地同它们及其后果分离开来的地方发展起来并摧毁自由伦理，那么必然的是：这个系统被有意识地接纳、在其权利上得到承认、被排除出高贵等级，并且给它让出一个特有的等级作为它的王国，在其中它可以固定下来，并在它的混乱以及通过另一种混乱来扬弃一种混乱中，展开它的全部活动。

由此，这个等级的级次就规定为，它处于一般的占有之中，也处于在此就占有而言可能的那种公正之中，它同时构成一个前后一贯的系统，并且由于占有的关系被接纳进形式的统一之中，每个个别者既然自在地能够占有，就对一切作为普遍者、或者说作为公民、在这个意义上作为 bourgeois 而发生关系，它为那种政治上的无足轻重，即按这种无足轻重这个等级的成员是私人，在和平与营利的果实中、在享受这些东西的完全安全中找到补偿，既就这种安全涉及个别的东西而言，也就它涉及这些东西的整体而言。
但对每个个别者来说，安全涉及整体，因为他在勇敢上被免除了，并且摆脱了那种属于第一个等级的必然性，即让自己去冒一种暴力死亡的危险，而这种危险对个别者来说就是一切享受、占有和权利的绝对不安全。

通过这种被扬弃的原则混合，以及这些原则被构成起来的、有意识的分离，每一个都得到自己的权利，并且唯独那个应当存在的东西被弄成了，即伦理作为绝对无差别的实在性，同时又正是同一个伦理作为在现存对立中的实在关系的实在性，以致后者被前者所征服，而这种征服本身也成为无差别的、得到和解的，——这种和解恰恰在于对必然性的认识，也在于伦理给予它的无机的自然和那些地下的力量的那种权利，因为它把自己的一部分让给它们、献给它们；因为献祭的力量就在于对同无机物的纠缠的直观和客观化，通过这种直观，这种纠缠被解开，无机物被分离开来，并且由于被认作这样的东西而由此本身也被接纳进无差别之中，而活的东西则由于把它作为自己的一部分所知道的东西放进其中并献给死亡，就同时承认了死亡的权利，同时又使自己从死亡中净化出来。

en: This is nothing other than the performance of the tragedy in the ethical, which the absolute eternally plays with itself — that it eternally gives birth to itself into objectivity, in this its shape thereby surrenders itself to suffering and death, and rises out of its ashes into glory.
The divine in its shape and objectivity has immediately a doubled nature, and its life is the absolute being-one of these natures.

But the movement of the absolute conflict of these two natures presents itself in the divine nature, which has grasped itself in it, as bravery, with which it frees itself from the death of the other conflicting nature, yet through this liberation gives its own life, for this life is only in the being-bound-together with this other, but just as absolutely rises again out of it, for in this death, as the sacrifice of the second nature, death is conquered; — but appearing in the other, the divine movement presents itself thus, that the pure abstraction of this nature, which would be a merely subterranean, pure negative power, is sublated through the living union with the divine, that the divine shines into it and through this ideal being-one in spirit makes it into its reconciled living body, which as the body at the same time remains in difference and in transitoriness and through the spirit beholds the divine as something foreign to itself — the image of this tragedy, more closely determined for the ethical, is the outcome of that process of the Eumenides as the powers of right that is in difference, and of Apollo, the god of indifferent light, over Orestes before the ethical organization, the people of Athens, — which humanly, as the Areopagus of Athens, casts equal votes into the urn of both powers, recognizes the coexistence of both, but does not thereby settle the strife and determines no relation and connection of them, but divinely, as the Athena of Athens, gives back wholly to this god the one entangled in difference by the god himself, and with the separation of the powers, which both had a share in the criminal, also effects the reconciliation in such a way that the Eumenides would be honoured by this people as divine powers and would now have their seat in the city, so that their wild nature would enjoy the intuition of Athena enthroned high on the acropolis opposite the altar erected to her below in the city, and would thereby be calmed.
zh: 这无非是那出在伦理的东西中上演的悲剧，绝对者永恒地与自己演出它，——即它永恒地把自己生进客观性，在它这个形态中因此把自己交给痛苦和死亡，又从自己的灰烬中升入荣耀。
神性的东西在它的形态和客观性中直接具有一种双重本性，而它的生命就是这些本性的绝对合一。

但这两个本性的绝对冲突的运动，在神性的那个本性那里——它在这冲突中已经以概念把握了自己——表现为勇敢：凭这种勇敢，它从另一个相冲突的本性的死亡中把自己解放出来，却通过这一解放交出自己的生命，因为这生命只有在与这另一个本性的联结中才存在，然而同样绝对地从它那里重新升起，因为在这种死亡中，作为第二个本性的献祭，死亡已被制服；——而在另一个本性那里出现时，神性的运动则这样呈现：这个本性的纯粹抽象，本来会是一种仅仅地下的、纯粹否定的力量，却通过和神性的活生生的联合而被扬弃了，神性照进它里面，并且通过精神中这种观念的合一，把它变成自己那已经和解的活生生的身体，这个身体作为身体同时留在差别中和易逝性中，并通过精神把神性的东西当作对它自己陌生的东西来直观，——这出悲剧的图像，就伦理的东西而言更切近地规定，就是那场诉讼的结局：欧墨尼得斯作为处于差别中的权利的各种力量，以及阿波罗这位无差别之光的神，在俄瑞斯忒斯身上、在伦理的组织即雅典人民面前的那场诉讼，——这个人民以人的方式作为雅典的阿瑞俄帕戈斯，把相等的票投入两个力量的票罐，承认两者并存，但这样一来并没有平息争执，也没有规定两者的任何关系和关联，可是以神的方式作为雅典的雅典娜，把那个被这位神自己卷入差别中的人完全交还给这位神，并且随着对那些两者在罪犯身上都有份的力量的区分，也这样进行和解：欧墨尼得斯会被这个人民当作神性的力量来尊敬，并且现在把它们的座位设在城里，以致它们那野性的本性得以享受对雅典娜的直观，而雅典娜高高坐在卫城上，与城中她下方为她设立的祭坛相对，它们也因此平静下来。

en: If tragedy consists in this, that ethical nature separates off from itself its inorganic [element] as a fate, so that it does not become entangled with it, and sets it over against itself, and, through the recognition of this fate in the struggle, is reconciled with the divine being as the unity of both, then, by contrast, in order to carry out this image, comedy in general will fall on the side of fatelessness; either that it [falls] within absolute aliveness and thus [represents] only shadow-images of oppositions or jests of struggles with a made fate and a fictitious enemy — or falls within non-aliveness and thus represents only shadow-images of self-subsistence and of absoluteness: the former the old or divine comedy, the latter the modern comedy.

The divine comedy is without fate and without true struggle, because in it the absolute confidence and certainty of the reality of the absolute is without opposition, and whatever as opposition brings a movement into this perfect security and rest is only a non-serious opposition having no inner truth — whether this opposition now presents itself against the divinity that appears foreign and external, yet stands there in absolute certainty, as the remnant or dream of a consciousness of isolated self-subsistence, also as a consciousness of one's own peculiarity that is indeed fixed and held fast, but the same in complete powerlessness and strengthlessness; or whether the opposition presents itself also in a self-felt and inwardly conscious divinity, which with consciousness generates for itself oppositions and plays, in which it with absolute levity stakes individual members of itself on the winning of a determinate prize and lets its manifold sides and moments give birth to themselves into perfect individuality and form themselves into organizations of their own, just as it on the whole can also take its movements, as a whole, not as movements against a fate but as contingencies, itself accounting itself invincible, counting loss for nothing, certain of absolute dominion over every peculiarity and extravagance, and conscious of what Plato says in another respect, that a polis has a nature strong to the point of admiration.

Such an ethical organization will thus, for example, without danger and fear or envy, drive individual members out to extremes of talent in every art and science and skill and make them into something particular therein, — sure of itself that such divine monstrosities do not harm the beauty of its shape, but are comic traits that brighten a moment of its shape.

As such cheerful exaltations of individual traits we shall, to cite a particular people, be able to regard Homer, Pindar, Aeschylus, Sophocles, Plato, Aristophanes etc., [shall] but also, both in the serious reaction against the increasingly serious particularization of Socrates and fully in the repentance over it, as [also] in the pullulating multitude and high energy of the individualizations simultaneously sprouting, not fail to recognize that the inner aliveness had thereby stepped out into its extremes, in the ripeness of these seed-corns announced its strength, but also the nearness of the death of this body that bore them, and had to take the oppositions, which it generally called forth and which it previously could itself excite and pursue in their more serious and far-reaching appearance, like wars, as contingencies and with equal levity, no longer for shadow-images but for an increasingly overpowering fate.
zh: 如果说悲剧在于：伦理的本性把它那无机的[东西]作为一种命运从自己身上分离出去并使之与自己相对立，为的是不与它纠缠在一起，并且通过在这场斗争中承认这命运，而与作为两者统一的神性本质和解了，那么相反，为了把这个图像展开，喜剧一般而言就会落到无命运性这一边；要么它[落到]绝对的生命性之内，因而只[表现]各种对立的阴影图像，或者与一种造出来的命运和一个虚构的敌人作斗争的玩笑——要么它落到非生命性之内，因而只表现独立性和绝对性的阴影图像：前者是古老的或神性的喜剧，后者是现代的喜剧。

神性的喜剧没有命运，也没有真正的斗争，因为在这种喜剧里，绝对者的实在性的绝对信赖和确定性是没有对立的，而凡是作为对立把一种运动带进这种完全的稳妥和安宁里的东西，都只是一种不严肃的、没有任何内在真理的对立，——这种对立不论是表现为与那种显得陌生而外在、却站在绝对确定性中的神性相对，作为孤立独立性的意识的一种残余或梦，也表现为一种虽然被固定住、被把持住的独自性的意识，但这意识处于完全的无力和无力气之中；或者这种对立也表现在一种自身感受到的、自身内自觉的神性中，这种神性有意识地为自己产生出对立和游戏，在游戏中它以绝对的轻率把自己的一些环节押在赢得某个规定好的奖赏上，并让自己那些杂多的方面和环节生成为完满的个体性、形成为自己的组织，就像它整体上也能把自己的那些运动，不是当作反对一种命运的运动，而是当作偶然性来看待，它自己认为自己不可战胜，把损失看作无，确信对每一种独自性和放纵拥有绝对统治，并且意识到柏拉图在另一层关系上所说的话：一个 Polis（城邦）有一种令人惊叹地强的本性。
这样一种伦理的组织就会例如毫无危险、恐惧或嫉妒地，把个别成员推向每一种艺术、科学和技能中才能的极端，并使他们在这方面成为某种特殊的东西，——它确信自身：这样一些神性的怪物并不损害它形态的美，反而是些喜剧性的特征，使它形态的某一个环节变得明朗。

作为对个别特征的这样一些明朗的高扬，我们要举一个特定的民族来说，就可以把荷马、品达、埃斯库罗斯、索福克勒斯、柏拉图、阿里斯托芬等等看作[这样的高扬]，但也会既在针对苏格拉底越来越严肃的特殊化的严肃反应中、完全在对这件事的悔恨中，也在同时萌发的个体化的孳生数量和高度能量中，不会看不出：内在的生命性由此已经[曾]踏入它的极端，在这些种子的成熟中宣告了自己的力量，但也宣告了承载它们的这个身体临近死亡，并且不得不把那些对立——它一般来说唤起了这些对立，而且事先还能以同样的轻率把它们在其更严肃、更广泛的外观中，如战争那样，当作偶然性来激起和推行——不再看作阴影图像，而是看作一种变得越来越占压倒优势的命运。

en: But on another side there is the other comedy, whose entanglements are without fate and without true struggle, because ethical nature is caught up in that itself; the knots here tie themselves not in playful oppositions but in oppositions that are serious for this ethical drive, yet comic for the spectator, and the rescue from them is sought in an affectation of character and absoluteness that constantly finds itself deceived and set aside.

The ethical drive (for it is not the conscious absolute ethical nature that plays in this comedy) must, to put it briefly, transform what exists into the formal and negative absoluteness of right and thereby give its fear the opinion of firmness for its possession, raise its belongings through treaties and contracts and all conceivable clauses into something secure and certain, deduce the systems about them from experience and reason, as certainty and necessity themselves, and ground them with the most profound reasonings, — but, as subterranean spirits in the poet saw the plantations they laid out in the hellish wastes swept away by the next storm-wind, so [must it see] half and whole sciences proven from experience and reason washed away by the next turn or even uprising of the earthly spirit, one system of right displaced by another, here humanity stepping into the place of harshness, there at the same time the will of power into the place of contractual security, and in the sciences as in actuality the best-won and most assured possessions of fundamental propositions and rights laid waste — and either think that it is its own efforts, hovering above fate with reason and will, that labour in such material and have brought about such changes, or else wax indignant over them as something unexpected and improper and first call upon all the gods against such necessity and then submit to it.

In both cases the ethical drive, which seeks an absolute infinity in these finitudes, gives only the farce of its faith and of its not-dying deception, which — darkest where it is brightest — is already in loss and wrong where it thinks to rest in the arms of justice, reliability and enjoyment itself.
zh: 但在另一方面，还有另一种喜剧，它的种种纠葛没有命运，也没有真正的斗争，因为伦理的本性本身就困在那里面；在这里，那些结不是系于游戏般的对立中，而是系于对这种伦理冲动来说严肃、对观众来说却可笑的对立中，而摆脱它们的得救，则被寻找于一种性格和绝对性的装腔作势里，这种装腔作势总是发现自己受了骗、被撇在一边。

伦理的冲动（因为在这种喜剧中演出的并不是有意识的绝对伦理本性）必须——简而言之——把现存的东西转化为权利的、形式的和否定的绝对性，并由此给自己的恐惧一种关于自己占有物之稳固的意见，通过条约和契约以及一切想得出来的附带条款，把自己的家当提升为某种可靠而确定的东西，把关于这些的系统从经验和理性、即从确定性和必然性本身演绎出来，并用最深奥的推理加以论证，——但是，正如诗人笔下的地下精灵眼看着它们在地狱荒野里栽种的作物被最近的一阵狂风刮走，它也同样眼看着由经验和理性证明过的半门和整门科学被最近的一次翻转、甚至大地精神的升起冲走，一种权利体系被另一种排挤掉，这里人道取代了严厉，那里同时又是权力的意志取代了契约的保障，并且在科学领域如同在现实性中一样，看到那些最正当获得、最有保障的根本命题和权利的占有被蹂躏，——并且要么认为，是它自己的、凭理性和意志悬在命运之上的努力，在这种材料中劳作，并产生了这样的变化，要么又把这些变化当作出乎意料的、不成体统的事情大发其火，先向一切神呼救以对抗这样的必然性，然后又顺从于它。
在两种情况下，这种在这些有限性中寻求一种绝对无限性的伦理冲动，都只是演出它的信仰和它那不死之欺骗的闹剧，——这种欺骗在最阴暗的地方恰恰最明亮——它已经在损失和不义之中，而它还以为自己正安歇在正义、可靠和享受本身的怀抱里。

en: Comedy separates the two zones of the ethical from one another in such a way that it lets each prevail purely for itself, that in the one the oppositions and the finite are a shadow without essence, but in the other the absolute is a deception.

But the true and absolute relation is that the one seriously shines into the other, that each [is] in bodily relation with the other, and that they are for one another mutually the serious fate; the absolute relation is therefore set up in tragedy.
zh: 喜剧把伦理的两个区域这样彼此分开：它让每一个都纯粹地自行其是，在一个区域里，各种对立和有限的东西是无本质的阴影，在另一个区域里，绝对者则是一种欺骗。
但真正而绝对的关系是：一个区域严肃地照进另一个区域，每一个都与另一个[是]处于身体性的关系中，并且它们彼此互为严肃的命运；所以这种绝对的关系是在悲剧中被建立起来的。

en: For although in the living shape or the organic totality of ethical life that which constitutes its real side is in the finite and therefore indeed cannot, in and for itself, take up its bodily essence perfectly into its divinity, yet it already expresses at itself its absolute idea, though distorted.

It indeed does not inwardly unite within itself, into absolute infinity, the moments of the same that are held apart as necessity, but has this unity only as an imitated negative self-subsistence, namely as the freedom of the individual; yet this real essence is absolutely bound to the absolute indifferent nature and shape of ethical life, and even if it must behold the same only as something foreign, it nevertheless beholds it and is one with it in spirit.

It is, even for the same, absolutely the first thing that the wholly pure and indifferent shape and the absolute ethical consciousness be, and the second is the indifferent matter that it, as the real, relate itself to it only as its empirical consciousness — just as it is the first thing that an absolute work of art be, and only the second whether this determinate individual be its author or merely beholds and enjoys the same.

As necessary as that existence of the absolute is, so necessary is also this distribution, that some be the living spirit, the absolute consciousness and the absolute indifference of the ideal and the real of ethical life itself, while others are its bodily and mortal soul and its empirical consciousness, which may not perfectly unite its absolute form and the inner essence, yet enjoys the absolute intuition as something, as it were, foreign to it, and, for real consciousness, is one with it through fear and trust as well as through obedience, but for ideal consciousness wholly unites itself with it in religion, in the common God and in his service.
zh: 因为尽管在伦理的活生生的形态或有机的总体性中，构成其实在方面的那个东西处在有限的东西中，因此虽然自在自为地不能把它的身体性本质完全接纳进它的神性里，它却已经在自身那里表露出它的绝对观念，不过是被扭曲地[表露出来]。
它虽然并不在自身内部把那些作为必然性而被分开的、伦理的环节联合成绝对的无限性，而只把这种统一当作一种模仿来的否定性独立性、即当作个别者的自由；但这个实在的本质却绝对地与伦理的绝对无差别的本性和形态结合在一起，即使它必须把后者只当作某种陌生的东西来直观，它也毕竟直观着它，并在精神中与它合一。
即使对它自己来说，绝对第一位的也是：完全纯粹而无差别的形态和绝对伦理的意识存在，而第二位的则是那无关紧要的事：它作为实在物，对前者只作为后者的经验意识而与之相关，——正如第一位的是一个绝对的艺术作品存在，而只是第二位的才是：这个特定的个别者是不是它的创作者，或者只是直观和享受它。

正如绝对者的那种存在是必然的，这种分配也是必然的：一部分是活生生的精神、绝对意识以及伦理本身观念物和实在物的绝对无差别，另一部分则是它的身体性的、会死的灵魂和它的经验意识，后者不允许把它的绝对形式和内在本质完全结合起来，却毕竟享受那绝对的直观——把它当作某种仿佛是它自己陌生的东西——，并且对实在的意识来说，通过恐惧和信任以及通过服从而与它合一，而对观念的意识来说，则在宗教中、在共同的神和对神的侍奉中完全与它结合。

en: But that which we have placed on one side under the external form of the first estate is the real absolute consciousness of ethical life.

It is consciousness and as such, on the negative side, pure infinity and the highest abstraction of freedom, i.e. the relation of subduing driven to its sublation, or free violent death; — on the positive side, however, consciousness is the singleness and particularity of the individual.

But this negative in itself, namely consciousness in general, of which the indicated distinctions are only its two sides, is absolutely taken up in a perfect way into the positive, its particularity and infinity or ideality absolutely into the universal and real, which being-one is the idea of the absolute life of ethical life.

In this being-one of infinity and reality in the ethical organization, the divine nature — of which Plato says that it is an immortal animal, whose soul and body, however, are born together for ever244) — appears to present the wealth of its manifoldness at the same time in the highest energy of infinity and unity, which becomes the wholly simple nature of the ideal element.

For even the most perfect mineral indeed presents in every part that is separated off from a mass the nature of the whole, but its ideal form is an outside-one-another both as the inner form of the fracture and as the outer form of crystallization; and not as in the elements of water, fire and air is every particular part the perfect nature and the representative of the whole, both as to essence and as to form or infinity.
No less is its real form also not penetrated by the true identity of infinity, but its senses have no consciousness.
Its light is a single colour and does not see; or if it is the indifference of the same, then there is no point of inhibition against their passage through itself.

Its sound resounds when struck by something foreign, but not out of itself; its taste does not taste, its smell does not smell, its heaviness and hardness do not feel; if it does not belong to the singleness of the determinations of sense but unites them in indifference, it is the undeveloped, closed absence of difference, not the unity that divides itself within itself and subjugates its division — just as the elements too, which are equal to themselves in all their parts, have in themselves only the possibility, not the actuality, of the differences, and only indifference under the form of quantity, not as indifference of what is qualitatively posited.

But the earth, as the organic and individual element, spreads itself out through the system of its shapes, from the first rigidity and individuality onwards, into the qualitative and difference, and first gathers itself, in the absolute indifference of ethical nature alone, into the perfect equality of all parts and the absolute real being-one of the individual with the absolute — into the first aether, which out of its self-same, fluid and soft form scatters its pure quantity through the individual formations into singleness and number, and thereby completely subdues this absolutely brittle and rebellious system in that number is purified into pure unity and into infinity and becomes intelligence, and thus the negative, in that it becomes absolutely negative — for the absolute concept is the absolute immediate opposite of itself, and the nothing is, as an ancient says245), no less than the something — can be perfectly one with the positively absolute; and in intelligence the form or the ideal is absolute form and as such real, and in absolute ethical life the absolute form is most truly united with the absolute substance.

Of the individualities of the formations that lie between the simple substance in reality as pure aether and it as the marriage with absolute infinity, none can bring the form and qualitative unity (whether through the quantitative, elemental equality of the whole and the parts, or in higher formations through the individualization going into the more singular of the parts) and at the same time the formal unification of the same into a whole (through the sociality of the leaves of plants, of sex, of herd life and the common labour of animals) to the absolute indifference with the essence and the substance that is in ethical life, because in intelligence alone individualization is driven to the absolute extreme, namely to the absolute concept, the negative to the absolutely negative, to be the unmediated opposite of itself.

This [intelligence], therefore, alone is capable, in that it is absolute singleness, of being absolute universality; in that it is absolute negation and subjectivity, of being absolute position and objectivity; in that it is absolute difference and infinity, of being absolute indifference, and the totality — actu in the unfolding of all oppositions and potentia in the absolute annulling and being-one of the same — of being the highest identity of reality and ideality.
zh: 但我们在第一个等级的外部形式之下放到一边的那个东西，是伦理的实在的绝对意识。
它是意识，并且作为意识，在否定的方面是纯粹的无限性和自由的最高抽象，即被推到其扬弃的征服关系，或者说自由的暴力性死亡；——但在肯定的方面，意识是个别者的单一性和特殊性。
但这个自在的否定东西，即一般而言的意识——上述那些区分只是它的两个方面——，以完善的方式被绝对地接纳进肯定的东西中，它的特殊性和无限性或观念性被绝对地接纳进普遍的东西和实在的东西中，这种合一就是伦理的绝对生命的观念。
在伦理的组织中这种无限性和实在性的合一里，神性的本性——柏拉图说它是一种不死的动物，但它的灵魂和身体是永远一起生出来的244)——显得同时以无限性和统一的最高能量来展示它杂多的丰富，这种能量成了观念元素的完全单纯的本性。
因为最完善的矿物虽然在被从一块质量上分出来的每一个部分中都呈现出整体的本性，但它的观念的形式无论作为断口的内部形式还是作为结晶的外部形式，都是一种彼此外在；而且并不像在水、火和空气的元素中那样，每一个特殊的部分都是整体的完善本性和代表，无论就本质还是就形式或无限性而言。
它那实在的形式也同样没有被无限性的真正同一性所贯穿，而是它的感官没有意识。
它的光是一种单一的颜色，并不看；或者如果它是各种颜色的无差别，那么就没有任何阻滞点来阻挡它们穿过它自身。

它的声音在被某种陌生的东西敲击时发出响声，但不是出自自身；它的味道不尝味，它的气味不嗅味，它的重量和硬度不感觉；如果它不属于感官规定的单一性，而是在无差别中把它们联合起来，那么它就是那未展开的、封闭的差别的缺失，而不是在自身中分裂自己并把自己的分裂置于轭下的统一，——正如那些在一切部分上都与自身相同的元素，在自身中只具有差别的可能性、而不是差别的现实性，并且只具有在量的形式之下的无差别，而不是作为被质性地设定之物的无差别。

但地球作为有机的、个体的元素，通过它的形态系统从最初的僵硬和个体性出发，扩展为质的东西和差别，并且只有在伦理本性的绝对无差别中才把自己归结为一切部分的完全相等和个别者与绝对者的绝对的实在合一，——归结为最初的以太：以太从它那自身相同的、流动而柔软的形式出发，通过那些个体的形成把自己的纯粹的量分散为单一性和数，并由此完全制服这个绝对脆硬而反叛的系统，因为数被提纯为纯粹的统一和无限性，成为智性，而否定东西也由此，即由于它变成绝对否定的东西——因为绝对概念是它自己的绝对直接的相反面，而无，正如一位古人245)所说，并不比某物少——，得以与肯定地绝对的东西完全合一；而在智性中，形式或观念物是绝对的形式，并且作为这样的东西是实在的，而在绝对伦理中，绝对的形式以最真正的方式与绝对的实体结合在一起。

在那些处于作为纯粹以太的实在性中的单纯实体与作为同绝对无限性联姻的它自身之间的形成物的个体性中，没有任何一个能把形式和质的统一（无论是通过整体与部分的量的、元素式的相等，还是在更高的形成物中通过深入到部分之更单一者中去的个体化）以及同时把它们的合形式为一个整体（通过植物叶子的社会性、性别、群居生活和动物的共同劳作），带到与伦理中那种本质和实体的绝对无差别，因为在智性中，唯独个体化被推到了绝对的极端，即被推到绝对概念，否定东西被推到绝对否定的东西，即成为它自己的无中介的相反面。
所以唯独它有能力，由于它是绝对的单一性，而成为绝对的普遍性；由于它是绝对的否定和主体性，而成为绝对的肯定和客观性；由于它是绝对的差别和无限性，而成为绝对的无差别，并且成为总体性——actu 在一切对立的展开中，potentia 在它们的绝对被消灭和合一中——成为实在性和观念性的最高同一性。

en: If the ether has cast out its absolute indifference into manifoldness in the differences of light, and in the flowers of the solar systems has given birth to its inner reason and totality into expansion, but those light-individuals are scattered in the multiplicity, while those which form the circling leaves of these must comport themselves in rigid individuality against them, and thus the unity of the former lacks the form of universality, the unity of the latter lacks pure unity, and neither of the two carries within itself the absolute concept as such, then in the system of ethical life the flower of the heavenly system unfolded into externality is folded back together, and the absolute individuals are perfectly united into universality, and reality or the body is at its highest one with the soul, because the real multiplicity of the body is itself nothing other than abstract ideality, the absolute concepts pure individuals, whereby these themselves are able to be the absolute system.

Therefore, if the absolute is this, that it intuits itself, and indeed as itself, and that absolute intuition and this self-cognition, that infinite expansion and this infinite taking-back of the same into itself, are absolutely one, then, if both are real as attributes, spirit is higher than nature; for if the latter is the absolute self-intuition and the actuality of infinitely differentiated mediation and unfolding, then spirit, which is the intuition of itself as itself or absolute cognition, is, in the taking-back of the universe into itself, both the out-thrown totality of this multiplicity, over which it reaches, and the absolute ideality of the same, in which it annihilates this externality and reflects itself into itself as the unmediated point of unity of the infinite concept.

From this idea of the nature of absolute ethical life there now results a relation of which we still have to speak, the relation of the ethical life of the individual to real absolute ethical life, and the relation of the sciences of the same, of morals and of natural law.

For since real absolute ethical life comprehends in itself, as united, infinity or the absolute concept, pure singularity, absolutely and in its highest abstraction, it is immediately the ethical life of the individual, and conversely the essence of the ethical life of the individual is absolutely the real and therefore universal absolute ethical life; the ethical life of the individual is a pulse-beat of the whole system and itself the whole system.

We note here also a hint on the part of language which, otherwise rejected, is fully justified by what precedes, namely that it lies in the nature of absolute ethical life to be a universal, or mores; that therefore the Greek word which designates ethical life and the German word express this nature of theirs excellently; but that the more recent systems of ethical life, since they make a being-for-self and singularity into the principle, cannot fail to display their relation in these words, and this inner hint proves itself so powerful that those systems, in order to designate their matter, could not misuse those words for that purpose, but adopted the word morality, which indeed, according to its origin, likewise points in that direction, but, because it is more a word first made, does not resist its inferior meaning so immediately.
zh: 如果说以太在光的诸无差别中把它的绝对无差别抛出去成了杂多，并且在诸太阳系的花朵里把它的内在理性和总体性生进延展之中，但那些光的个体却分散在繁多之中，而那些构成它们的旋转叶片的个体则必须在僵硬的个体性中与这些光的个体相对待，于是前者的统一性缺少普遍性的形式，后者的统一性缺少纯粹的统一性，而两者中没有一个在自身中承载着绝对概念本身，那么，在伦理的体系中，天界体系那向外展开的花朵就被收拢折叠起来，那些绝对的个体被完全统一进普遍性之中，而实在性或身体则最高程度地与灵魂为一，因为身体自身的实在的杂多不是别的，正是抽象的观念性，那些绝对的概念是纯粹的个体，由此这些个体本身才可能成为绝对体系。

所以，如果绝对者是这样的东西，即它直观自己，而且是作为自己来直观自己，并且那种绝对的直观与这种自我认识、那种无限的展开与这种把这一展开无限地收回自身之中，绝对是同一个东西，那么，当两者作为属性都是实在的时，精神就高于自然；因为如果自然是绝对的自我直观，是无限地分化了的中介和展开的现实性，那么，精神——它是把自身作为自身来直观，或者说，它是绝对的认识——在把宇宙收回自身之中时，就既是这种繁多的向外抛出的总体性（精神超出这一总体性之上而统摄它），又是这种繁多的绝对观念性，精神在这种观念性中消灭这个彼此外在，并把自己反思为无限概念的无中介的统一点。
从绝对伦理的本性的这一观念中，现在产生出一种还必须谈一谈的关系，即单个的人的伦理与实在的绝对伦理的关系，以及它的各门科学即道德学和自然法之间的关系。
因为实在的绝对伦理把无限性或绝对概念、纯粹的单个性在自身中统一地以概念把握起来，而且是绝对地、在它的最高抽象中这样来把握，所以它直接就是单个的人的伦理；反过来，单个的人的伦理的本质绝对就是实在的、因而是普遍的绝对伦理；单个的人的伦理是整个体系的一次脉搏跳动，并且本身就是整个体系。

我们在这里也注意到语言的一种暗示，这种暗示平时遭到弃置，从前面所说的却得到完全的辩护，即：绝对伦理的本性就在于它是一种普遍的东西或习俗（Sitten）；因此，标示伦理的那个希腊词和那个德语词都极好地表达出伦理的这种本性；但那些较新的伦理体系，由于它们把自为存在和单一性当作原则，不可能不在这些词上把它们的关联摆出来，而这种内在的暗示表现得如此有力，以致那些体系为了标示它们的事情，无法为此滥用这些词，而是采用了道德这个词，后者按它的来源虽然也同样指向那个方向，但因为它更多是一个才造出来的词，就不那么直接地抗拒它较差的意义。

en: But absolute ethical life, according to what has been said so far, is so essentially the ethical life of all that one cannot say of it that it mirrors itself as such on the individual; for it is just as much his essence as the ether pervading nature is the inseparable essence of the shapes of nature, and as the ideality of their appearing forms, space, is not particularized in any one of them absolutely for nothing; on the contrary, just as the lines and corners of the crystal, in which it expresses the outer form of its nature, are negations, so ethical life, insofar as it expresses itself on the individual as such, is a negative.
In the first place it cannot express itself in the individual if it is not his soul, and it is that only insofar as it is a universal and the pure spirit of a people.

The positive is by nature earlier than the negative, or, as Aristotle puts it, the people is by nature earlier than the individual; for if the individual taken in separation is nothing self-subsistent, he must, like all the parts, be in a unity with the whole; but whoever cannot be communal or, out of self-subsistence, needs nothing, is no part of the people and therefore either beast or god.246) Then, insofar as it expresses itself in the individual as such, it is posited under the form of negation, that is, it is the possibility of the universal spirit, and the ethical qualities that belong to the individual, such as courage or moderation or thrift or liberality etc., are negative ethical life — namely that in the particularity of the individual no singularity is truly fixed and no real abstraction is made — and possibilities or capacities to be in universal ethical life.

These virtues, which in themselves are possibilities and are of a negative meaning, are the object of morals, and one sees that the relation of natural law and of morals has in this way been reversed, namely that to morals there falls only the domain of what is in itself negative, but to natural law the truly positive, according to its name, that it is to construct how ethical nature attains its true right; whereas — if both the negative and this positive were to express, as the abstraction of externality, of the formal ethical law, of the pure will and of the will of the individual, and then the syntheses of these abstractions such as coercion, the restriction of the freedom of the individual through the concept of universal freedom, etc., the determination of natural law — it would be a natural wrong, since, when such negations are taken as realities, ethical nature is put into the highest ruin and misfortune.
zh: 但绝对伦理按照前面所说的，如此本质地是一切人的伦理，以致人们不能说它作为这样的东西在单个的人身上映照出来；因为它如此地就是单个的人的本质，正如渗透自然的以太是自然诸形态不可分离的本质，也正如它们那些显现形态的观念性即空间，不会在任何形态中绝对地、无缘无故地使自己特殊化；相反，正如晶体的线条和角——晶体在这些线条和角中表达出它本性的外部形式——是否定，伦理在它于作为这样的单个者身上表达出来时，也是一个否定的东西。
首先，如果它不是单个的人的灵魂，它就不能在单个的人身上表达出来，而它只有在它是普遍的东西、是一个民族的纯粹精神时，才是灵魂。

肯定的东西按本性比否定的东西更早，或者像亚里士多德所说的，民族按本性比单个的人更早；因为如果单个的人孤立起来不是什么独立的东西，那他就必须像所有部分一样处在与整体的统一之中；但谁不能过共同的生活，或者出于独立性而什么都不需要，谁就不是民族的一部分，因而要么是野兽，要么是神246)；其次，就伦理在作为这样的单个者身上表达出来而言，它是被设定在否定的形式之下的，也就是说，它是普遍精神的可能性，而那些属于单个的人的伦理品质，如勇敢、节制、节俭或慷慨等等，则是否定的伦理——即：在单个的人的特殊性中并没有真正把一种单一性固定下来，也没有作出一种实在的抽象——并且是存在于普遍伦理之中的可能性和能力。

这些德性自在就是可能性、并且只有一种否定的含义，它们是道德学的对象；人们看到，自然法和道德学的关系以这种方式颠倒了过来，即道德学只分得自在的否定的东西这一领域，自然法却分得真正肯定的东西，按其名称，它应当建构的是伦理本性如何达到它真正的权利；反之——如果无论那个否定的东西还是这个肯定的东西，都被表达为外在性、形式的伦理法则、纯粹意志和单个的人的意志的抽象，随后这些抽象的综合如强制、通过普遍自由的概念对单个的人的自由所作的限制等等，都被表达为自然法的规定——那就会是一种自然的非权利，因为在这种把这样的否定当作实在性来作为基础的做法中，伦理本性就被置入最高的败坏和不幸之中。

en: But just as these qualities are the reflection of absolute ethical life in the individual as the negative, but the individual which is in absolute indifference with the universal and the whole, thus its reflection in its pure consciousness, so too a reflection of the same must be present in its empirical consciousness, and such a reflection must constitute the ethical nature of the second estate, which is in fixed reality, in possession and property and outside courage.

It is now this reflection of the same for which the ordinary meaning of morality can more or less fit — the formal setting-into-indifference of the determinacies of the relation, thus the ethical life of the bourgeois or of the private person, for whom the difference of the relations is fixed and who depends on them and is in them.

A science of this morality is accordingly, to begin with, the cognition of these relations themselves, so that, insofar as they are considered in reference to the ethical, since this reference, on account of absolute fixedness, can only be formal, precisely that uttering of tautology mentioned above finds its place here: this relation is only this relation; if you are in this relation, then be, in the reference to it, in it; for if in actions which have references to this relation you do not act in reference to it, then you annihilate, then you sublate it.

The true sense of this tautology at the same time immediately includes that this relation itself is nothing absolute and therefore also the morality that goes to it is something dependent and nothing truly ethical, which true sense, according to the above, follows from the fact that only the form of the concept, the analytic unity, is the absolute and therefore negatively absolute because of the content, which, as something determinate, contradicts the form.
zh: 但正如这些品质是绝对伦理在单个的人身上——作为否定的东西、但又是处在与普遍的东西和整体的绝对无差别之中的单个的人——的映现，也就是它在它的纯粹意识中的映现，同样，也必定有一种这些品质的映现存在于它的经验意识之中，而这种映现必定构成第二个等级的伦理本性，这个等级处在固定不移的实在性中，处在占有和财产中，并且处在勇敢之外。
正是这些品质的这一映现，才是道德的通常含义或多或少能够适合的东西，——即把诸关系的规定性形式地设定为无差别，也就是资产者（bourgeois）或私人的伦理，对他们来说诸关系的差别是固定的，他们依赖于这些关系并处在这些关系之中。
关于这种道德的一门科学因此首先就是对这些关系本身的认识，所以，当这些关系被放在与伦理的东西的关联中考察时——由于这种关联出于绝对被固定的缘故而只能是形式的——上面提到的那种同义反复的说法在这里就有了它的位置：这个关系只是这个关系；如果你处在这个关系中，那就在对它的关联中处在它之中；因为如果你在对这个关系有所关联的行动中不是在对它的关联中行动，那你就是在消灭它，就是在扬弃它。
这种同义反复的真正意义同时直接包含着：这个关系本身并不是什么绝对的东西，因此那种针对它的道德也是某种依赖性的东西，并不是真正伦理的东西；按照上面所说的，这一真正意义由此得出：只有概念的形式、分析性的统一才是绝对者，并且正因为内容之故才是否定意义上的绝对者，而内容作为某种被规定的东西与形式相矛盾。

en: But those qualities which are truly ethical, in that in them the particular or the negative appears, purely taken up into indifference, can be called ethical qualities, and only then virtues, when they individualize themselves again in a higher energy and, though within absolute ethical life, become as it were proper living shapes, like the virtues of an Epaminondas, Hannibal, Caesar and a few others.

As such energies they are shapes and therefore not absolute in themselves, no more than the shapes of the other organic formations, but the stronger emergence of one side of the idea of the whole; and the morals of the virtues, or — if we want to determine morals quite generally in relation to morality and if for the presentation of virtue the name ethics were adopted — ethics must therefore be only a natural description of the virtues.
zh: 但那些真正伦理的品质——由于特殊的东西或否定的东西在其中显现出来，它们被纯粹地接纳进无差别之中——可以叫做伦理的品质，并且只有当它们在一种更高的能量中重新个体化，并且在绝对伦理之内仿佛成为特有的、活生生的形态，像伊巴密浓达、汉尼拔、恺撒以及另外一些人的德性那样，才叫做德性。
作为这样的能量，它们是形态，因而自在并不是绝对的，正如其他有机形成的诸形态也不是绝对的，而是整体的观念中某一方面的更强的凸显；而各德性的道德学，或者——如果我们想一般地把道德学规定为与道德相对的东西，并且为德性的描述采用伦理学这个名称——伦理学，因此就必须只是一种对诸德性的自然描述。

en: Now just as this ethics has a reference to the subjective or negative, so the negative in general must be distinguished as the persistence of difference and as the lack of the same; it is that first negative of which we spoke before, but this other negative, the lack of difference, represents totality as something enveloped and undeveloped, in which movement and infinity in their reality are not.

The living thing under this form of the negative is the becoming of ethical life, and education according to its determinacy the appearing, progressive sublation of the negative or subjective; for the child, as the form of the possibility of an ethical individual, is something subjective or negative, whose coming of age is the ceasing of this form and whose education is the discipline or the subduing of the same; but the positive and the essence is that it, nourished at the breast of universal ethical life, lives in its absolute intuition at first as [in that] of a foreign essence, comprehends it ever more, and thus passes over into the universal spirit.

It is evident from this of itself that those virtues, as well as absolute ethical life, no more than the becoming of the same through education, are a striving after a peculiar and separate ethical life, and that the effort after a peculiar positive ethical life is something futile and in itself impossible, and that in regard to ethical life the word of the wisest men of antiquity alone is true: be ethical, [namely] to live according to the customs of one's country — and in regard to education [the word] which a Pythagorean answered to someone who asked what would be the best education for his son: if you make him a citizen of a well-ordered people247)
zh: 现在，正如这种伦理学与主观的东西或否定的东西有关联一样，否定的东西一般而言必须被区分为差别的持存和差别的缺乏；前面说到的是那第一个否定的东西，而这另一个否定的东西，即差别的缺乏，则把总体性表象为一个被包裹起来的、未展开的东西，其中并没有处在它的实在性中的运动和无限性。

在这种否定的形式之下的活的东西，就是伦理的生成，而按其规定性来说，教育则是这种否定的东西或主观的东西的显现着的、不断前进的扬弃，因为孩子作为伦理个体的可能性的形式，是某种主观的东西或否定的东西，他长大成人就是这种形式的终止，他的教育就是对这种形式的管教或制服；而肯定的东西和本质则在于：他在普遍伦理的胸前受到哺育，起初在它的绝对直观中作为对一个异己本质的直观而生活，越来越多地以概念把握它，并这样过渡到普遍精神之中。
从这里自然可以看出：那些德性以及绝对伦理，和它们通过教育而生成一样，同样都不是对一种特有的、分离的伦理的追求，而且追求一种特有的、肯定的伦理是某种徒劳的、自在不可能的事情；在伦理方面，只有古代那些最智慧的人的话才是真的：合乎伦理，就是按照自己国家的习俗生活——而在教育方面，则是一个毕达哥拉斯派的人对那个问他什么是对他儿子最好的教育的人所回答的话：如果你把他造就成一个秩序良好的民族的公民247)

en: If thus the absolutely ethical has its own organic body in the individuals, and its movement and liveliness in the common being and doing of all is absolutely identical as universal and particular, and we have considered it in particularity, but in such a way that its essence is the absolutely identical, and indeed generally in that identity, then it must also present itself in the form of universality and of cognition, as a system of legislation — so that this system fully expresses reality or the living existing mores, so that it does not happen, as is often the case, that what is right in a people and is actual cannot be cognized from its laws, which clumsiness of bringing the true mores into the form of laws, and the fear of thinking these mores, of viewing and confessing them as one's own, is the sign of barbarism.

But this ideality of the mores and their form of universality in the laws must, insofar as it subsists as ideality, at the same time be perfectly united again with the form of particularity, and thus the ideality as such must receive a pure absolute shape, and thus be intuited and worshipped as the god of the people, and this intuition must itself again have its activity and joyful movement in a cultus.
zh: 如果绝对伦理的东西这样在诸个体身上有它特有的有机身体，并且它在一切人的共同存在和行动中的运动和生动性作为普遍的东西和特殊的东西是绝对同一的，而我们是在特殊性中、但又是这样来看它，即它的本质是绝对同一的东西，并且一般地是在那种同一性中来看它，那么，它也必须在普遍性和认识的形式中、作为立法的体系把自己表象出来——以致这个体系完全表达出实在性或者活生生地现存的习俗，从而使下面这种情况不致发生（而这种情况是常有的）：在一个民族中什么是正当的、什么是现实存在的，却不能从它的法律中得到认识；而把真正的习俗带进法律形式的这种笨拙，以及害怕去思考这些习俗、把它们看作并承认为自己的东西的那种畏惧，正是野蛮的标志。
但这种习俗的观念性和它们在法律中的普遍性形式，在它作为观念性而持存的情况下，必须同时重新与特殊性的形式完全结合起来，从而使观念性作为这样的东西获得一种纯粹的绝对形态，因而作为民族之神被直观和被崇拜，而这种直观本身又必须在一个崇拜仪式中有它的活跃和欢乐的运动。
